issue.fhir_comments: RFC 6657 section 3 leaves every text/* registration that does not say how the charset is determined defaulting to US-ASCII. So for a text/* type whose registration a server has not read, the absence of a charset may mean 'any charset' - in which case the bare form subsumes - or may mean 'US-ASCII', in which case the two are disjoint. The two readings give opposite answers, so no answer may be given

details.fhir_comments: wording varies by server; it must name both codes and identify charset as what it could not judge
